title: Go: Template Engine
description: Build a template engine with custom delimiters, variables, loops, conditionals, and filters inspired by text/template.

steps.title: Parse variable placeholders
steps.description: Write a `Parse(tmpl string) (*Template, error)` function that finds `{{var}}` patterns using regex and stores the variable names. Implement `Render(ctx map[string]string) string` to replace `{{var}}` with values from the context. Print the rendered output of `"Hello {{name}}"` with `ctx["name"] = "World"`.
hints: `Template` struct stores the raw template and parsed variable names.

steps.title: Custom delimiters
steps.description: Extend `Parse` to accept custom `open` and `close` delimiters via `ParseWithDelims(tmpl, open, close string)`. Default to `{{` and `}}`. Print the result of parsing with `[%` and `%]` delimiters, e.g. `"Hi [%name%]"`.
hints: Store delimiters in the Template struct.
Escape regex metacharacters in delimiters with `regexp.QuoteMeta`.
Build the regex pattern dynamically: `open + "([^" + close[0:1] + "]+)" + close`.

verification.failureMessage: Check that delimiters are regex-escaped correctly.

steps.title: If blocks
steps.description: Implement `{% if var %}...{% endif %}` blocks. Render the block content only if the variable is non-empty. Print the result of `"A{% if show %}B{% endif %}C"` with `show` set to `"true"` and then `""` (empty).
hints: Parse nested blocks with stack-based or recursive descent parsing.
Use `strings.Contains` on the rendered variable value for truthiness.

verification.failureMessage: Check that empty/zero values skip the block.

steps.title: For loops
steps.description: Implement `{% for item in items %}...{% endfor %}` where `items` is a comma-separated string. Inside the loop, render `{{item}}` with each value. Print the result of `"{% for x in list %}{{x}} {% endfor %}"` with `list = "a,b,c"`.
hints: Split `items` by comma to get the slice.
Replace `{{item}}` inside the loop body for each iteration.
Build the full output by concatenating iteration results.

verification.failureMessage: Expected 'a b c' from the loop output.

steps.title: Custom filters (upper, lower)
steps.description: Extend variable syntax to support filters: `{{var | upper}}` and `{{var | lower}}`. Apply the filter to the value before interpolation. Print `"{{name | upper}}"` with `name = "john"` and `"Hello {{name | lower}}"` with `name = "WORLD"`.
hints: Parse filter names after `|` in the variable expression.
Store a `map[string]func(string) string` of available filters.
Chain multiple filters: split on `|`, apply left to right.

verification.failureMessage: Check that 'upper' and 'lower' filters are registered and applied.

steps.title: Template nesting and inheritance
steps.description: Implement `{% extends "base" %}` and `{% block name %}...{% endblock %}`. The base template contains `{% block body %}{% endblock %}` and child templates fill blocks. Render a child template that extends a simple base. Print the composed output.
hints: When parsing `{% extends %}`, load the base template and overlay block content.
Use `strings.Replace` to substitute block content into the base.

verification.failureMessage: Ensure the base template is loaded and blocks are overlaid.
